target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)

family.contrast: added to the candidate: the daily as-of distance from the rolling satiation level as one term, against the candidate (the nested contrast of #1483's question 1, default 1)

columns.satiation_dist_roll: the reserves-to-assets ratio the as-of rule reads at the row's own decision minus the rolling level at that row; the term is the column in percentage points (times 100)
columns.satiation_hinge_roll: the percentage points by which that ratio is below the level, 0 at or above it (already in percentage points)

family.units: percentage points of the reserves-to-assets ratio, chosen before any score and not tuned; the ridge of 5 is the candidate's and is not changed for the new term

alignment: The term of a training pair with target row T at lead h is the column at row T - h, the decision row of the direct pair; the term of a forecast made at decision row d is the column at row d, whatever the lead (the same rows as repo_model.s3c_h9.TargetForecastTable). A column value is public at its own row's decision (zero lag, sources_measurement.json satiation_distance_columns) so the training pair reads nothing after its own decision. A training pair whose decision row has no value raises ValueError; a forecast whose decision row has none enters at 0.

prechecks.note: Made at the 18:00 instant before the walk and reported on the page (the ruling asks for both, from findings #621 and #622 as #1505 relays them). They are measurements of the columns, not conditions of the run.
prechecks.621: the share of rows with the hinge on (ratio below the rolling level), by calendar year, on the release-dated build at 18:00: a rolling level that acts as a two-year reserves low shows the hinge on in years with no pressure (2022 and 2023 on the first build)
prechecks.622: the same columns built on the weekly H.4.1 lag and on the per-release read, both at 18:00: the rows on which the distance differs (median and largest, in percentage points) and the days on which the hinge switches on or off differently; the weekly lag is the older read, so the difference is staleness and not leakage
prechecks.no_future: satiation.check_distance_no_future on the rows of the built columns, every row, at 18:00 (LookAheadError on a value that depends on a later row)

frame.windows: the two windows of #1255, loaded as #1483 loads them: the development window (decision days whose five targets fall on or before 2025-12-31) and the 2026 development days (five targets from 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-03). The 2026 days are reported on their own, as a window
frame.walk: one sc.walk per window with the candidate and the two arms, which share the base fit and #941's pool; the arms are compared on the same days. The study refuses to write a record unless every scored decision day has a forecast of every arm
frame.guards: a scored decision day or target day passes lockbox.require_unlocked through spread_mean_reversion_686.require_scored_days with the last day of the window; the blind tier (from 2026-09-04) and every lockbox day are refused
frame.reproduction: the candidate, (s3) and (s3c) are re-run in the same walk; their pooled means are written beside #1483's record (against_1483) and are expected to agree to rounding, which shows the control is #1483's

inputs: the published panel (digest 4ddc3882cd6d406b11e1088f8ff6195e16dde175a0ad6818abe40dd5bdac8999, built at 18:00) and the scratch panel of scripts/pressure_v1_1.py panel --end 2026-09-03 (same dates, plus bank_total_assets), from which only the two distance columns are built; the study refuses a scratch panel whose dates or published columns differ from the published panel's

primary.metric: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5
primary.also_reported: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp) and the coverage of the central 90% band, as in #1483
primary.splits: pooled, by lead, by regime and by pressure-day type of the target day; groups of fewer than 20 days are listed and not tested

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1483 (#1483's, so the settings are the ablation's), two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009): the family helps when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, hurts when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided

reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c-ann-net) stays the candidate until she rules.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the lead, regime and pressure-day-type splits beside it.

The row does not mark or re-mark H5.M3. If it changes what the milestone's caveat says, the page and the pull request put that to her as a marked question with numbered options and a default that changes no claim.
